questions.prompt: Plan an investigation into how the surface affects friction, using a ramp and a wooden block.
questions.modelAnswer: Independent variable: the surface on the ramp (glass, wood, cloth, sandpaper). Dependent variable: the angle at which the block starts to slide, measured with a protractor. Control variables: the same block, the same mass, the same ramp length, raising the ramp slowly each time. Repeat each surface three times and average. Prediction: rougher surfaces need a bigger angle.
rubric: Dependent variable: slip angle (or force) and how it is measured

questions.prompt: Planes, cars and fish have streamlined shapes to reduce…
questions.explain: Drag is the friction force from fluids (air or water). Streamlining reduces it.

questions.text: A substance that reduces friction, like oil or grease, is called a ___. Friction produces ___, which is why rubbing your hands warms them.
questions.explain: Lubricants reduce friction; friction turns some energy into heat.

questions.prompt: Friction wears out tyres, shoes and machine parts, costing money. Would a world without friction be better? Argue both sides and give a conclusion.
questions.modelAnswer: Without friction machines would not wear out and would waste less energy as heat, which saves money and fuel. But we could not walk, hold a pen, brake a vehicle or even keep objects on a table, since everything would slide. Nails and knots would not hold. Overall, friction is necessary; the goal is to control it: increase it where we need grip and reduce it with lubricants and wheels where it wastes energy.
